relevance_replay.rationale: The selected dimensions cover the monitoring infrastructure decisions directly needed after deployment: what evidence to collect; how much trajectory, action, outcome, policy, and reasoning context to retain; how monitoring is implemented and scaled; how alerts and escalation operate; how quality, drift, fairness, safety, reward hacking, and anomalous behavior are detected; how monitoring results are evaluated and fed back; who reviews and acts on findings; and how detected problems trigger adaptation, runtime intervention, rollback, recovery, and recovery verification. Serving, access control, runtime validation, and safety constraints are included because they constrain the availability, integrity, and operational use of monitoring. Dimension 29 is the only dimension dropped because it is predominantly about training-time policy optimization rather than post-deployment monitoring infrastructure.

values.label: Business-rule validation

clusters.name: Policy Adaptation Strategy

values.label: Periodic model retraining

values.label: Fine-tuning and domain adaptation

values.label: Online continual learning

values.label: Prompt-template adjustment

values.label: User-specific adaptation

values.label: Historical-sample rehearsal cache

values.label: Reduced factual drift
values.description: Continual pre-training improves freshness of facts and trends in changing domains.

values.label: Base-model preservation
values.description: Adapter-based updates preserve most base parameters while adjusting deployed outputs for new conditions.

values.label: Accelerated model deployment
values.description: Feedback-driven adaptation can reduce launch time and streamline deployment.

clusters.name: Post-Deployment Recovery Mechanism
clusters.description: Which mechanism restores, rolls back, or heals a deployed agent after faults or degraded behavior?

values.label: Registry-based rollback
values.description: Restore a deployed agent by automatically switching to a known-good registered version when monitoring detects degraded behavior. This option centers recovery on deployment-version reversal rather than on restoring runtime state or healing the agent in place.

includes.label: Registry-based automated rollback
includes.description: Use a known-good registry version and automated workflow triggers to reverse a problematic deployment.

values.label: Integrated stateful self-healing recovery
values.description: Recover the agent through a coordinated mechanism that combines persistent checkpoints, automatic healing, registry-based rollback, and restoration of stateful model state. This option supports recovery when simply changing the deployed version is insufficient because the agent's runtime or learned state is also compromised.

includes.label: Checkpoint persistence
includes.description: Retain recoverable agent checkpoints across training or deployment timesteps.

includes.label: Automatic healing and recovery
includes.description: Detect faults and resume operation through automatic healing without manual resets.

includes.label: Registry-based automated rollback
includes.description: Use a known-good registry version and automated workflow triggers to reverse a problematic deployment.

includes.label: State restoration during rollback

values.label: Recovery and rollback operational complexity

values.label: Continued operation without manual reset

values.label: Automated rollback drills
